nodes.title: CM class functions and analytic heights
nodes.statement: For the profinite absolute Galois group Γ_Q, CM⁰ consists of rational-valued locally constant conjugation-invariant functions a for which a(σ)+a(cσ) is constant. For a CM algebra E and type Φ, put a_Φ(σ)=#(Φ∩σΦ) and a⁰_Φ equal to its conjugacy average, computed in any finite Galois quotient through which the action factors. Expand a in finite-image irreducible Artin characters and set Z̃(a)=−Σ_η a_η((L_f′/L_f)(0,η)+(log f_η)/2). Define h_Col(E,Φ)=Z̃(a⁰_Φ). Every nontrivial character occurring is totally odd; the trivial term uses ζ(0) and ζ′(0). Define H_CM⊂CM⁰ to be the Q-span, over all CM pairs, of a⁰_Φ. It is the domain determined by total Faltings heights. Every generator is invariant under σ↦σ⁻¹ and vanishes at complex conjugation c; consequently H_CM is a proper subspace of CM⁰, since the constant function 1 does not vanish at c.
proofSteps: Pass to a finite splitting Galois group and take its normalized conjugacy sum; prove independence under refinement.
Use the c-parity decomposition to exclude nontrivial even constituents and import regularity and nonvanishing at 0 for the remaining Artin characters.
Use conductor-compatible induction and the real structure to show Z̃(a) is real. General Artin holomorphy is not an input.
acceptance: The complement identity for a⁰_Φ has constant d, and h_Col is additive on product CM pairs.

nodes.title: CM-height invariance and Colmez linearity
nodes.statement: For a maximal-order CM pair (E,Φ), stable unscaled Faltings height depends only on that pair. For product CM algebras extend height additively. There is a unique Q-linear map ht_H:H_CM→R with ht_H(a⁰_Φ)=h_Falt(E,Φ). Inducing a field type to a CM overfield Ẽ multiplies a⁰ by [Ẽ:E]. Uniqueness here is only on the overlap span H_CM. Colmez’s period-normalized functional on all CM⁰ requires its component-period values and a sign/conductor/metric adapter; total heights alone do not specify that extension. The individual height conjecture on H_CM remains unproved and unused.
proofSteps: Import potential good reduction and model independence from the CM/height owners.

Use Colmez Theorem 0.3 on the component-character generators, whose period values specify the full functional, to establish compatibility of total-height linear relations after the sign/conductor/metric normalization. Restrict to H_CM; its spanning property gives uniqueness there. The complete period-comparison proof and normalization adapter remain G-Colmez.
Prove the induction scaling by counting extensions of embeddings, then extend products by additivity.
acceptance: Conjugating the CM action preserves the height; no individual equality with h_Col is inferred.

Evaluation at c annihilates H_CM and is nonzero on CM⁰. Adding any real multiple of that evaluation to an extension leaves its total-height values unchanged; reject unrestricted uniqueness from total heights alone.

nodes.title: Average CM character
nodes.statement: For a CM field E/F with [F:Q]=d≥1 and χ=χ_E/F, (1/(2d))Σ_{Φ∈CM(E)}a⁰_Φ=2^(d−2)(1+(1/d)Ind_{Γ_F}^{Γ_Q}χ). Consequently 2^(−d)Σ_Φ h_Col(E,Φ)=−(L_f′/L_f)(0,χ)/2−log(D_E/D_F)/4−d log(2π)/2. The sums contain all 2^d types with multiplicity one.
proofSteps: Count types containing any specified embedding and pair of embeddings in the finite Galois closure; average conjugates.
Apply Z̃ and Artin induction to the quadratic Hecke character.
Use ζ′(0)/ζ(0)=log(2π) and conductor(Indχ)=D_F N_F/Q(d_E/F)=D_E/D_F.
acceptance: For d=1 the character identity reads (1+χ)/2; for d=2 it reads 1+(Indχ)/2.

nodes.title: The CM height torus
nodes.statement: Given a CM field E/F of degree 2d and an embedding ι₀:E→C, form T=Res_E G_m/ker(N_F/Q) and T_so=ker(N_E/F). The map z↦z/z̄ identifies T/(Res_F G_m/ker N_F/Q) with T_so. The kernel subtorus is identified with G_m by N_F/Q; the diagonal G_m→T instead has kernel μ_d. Character vectors of T have a_ι+a_cι independent of ι. The distinguished cocharacter selects ι₀ and has reflex norm the quotient Res_E G_m→T.
proofSteps: Use the existing quotient-torus and character-lattice equivalence.
Compute the annihilator of ker N_F/Q and the quotient by Res_F G_m.
Pair the distinguished cocharacter with each embedding character to determine its reflex norm.
acceptance: The torus has dimension d+1 and T_so has dimension d; the scalar-kernel map is distinguished from the diagonal.

nodes.statement: For each p let K_so,p be the image of (O_E⊗Z_p)× in (E⊗Q_p)×/(F⊗Q_p)×=T_so(Q_p). nodes.title: The total reflex CM pair
nodes.statement: Let E♯ be the finite étale Q-algebra whose embedding Γ_Q-set is CM(E). Complementing a type is its CM involution, so E♯ is a product of CM fields of total degree 2^d. For a chosen ι₀, Φ♯ consists of the types containing ι₀ and has size 2^(d−1). Its T-representation H♯=E♯ has character pullback [Φ]↦Σ_{ι∈Φ}[ι]. Choose ξ∈E♯× with ξ̄=−ξ and Im ι_Φ(ξ)>0 for Φ containing ι₀; after multiplying ξ by a positive integer so that ψ(x,y)=Tr(ξxȳ) is integral on O_E♯, this form polarizes H♯, giving an abelian scheme A♯/Y₀ of dimension 2^(d−1). Its maximal-order lattice is O_E♯.
proofSteps: Use finite étale Galois descent on the finite set of CM types.
Use complement and the half-set containing ι₀ to define the CM algebra and type.

Use the CM-type character vectors to descend the T-action; weak approximation supplies ξ. Clear the denominators of ψ on the maximal-order lattice by a positive integer, preserving all positivity conditions.
Apply the polarized-CM family theorem and extend by the good-reduction criterion.
acceptance: A nontransitive CM-type Γ_Q-set yields a product algebra, with no forced field instance.

nodes.statement: The total reflex pair decomposes as the product of reflex pairs indexed by Γ_Q-orbits of CM(E). Its class function satisfies a⁰_(E♯,Φ♯)=(1/(2d))Σ_Φ a⁰_(E,Φ), hence h_Falt(E♯,Φ♯)=(1/(2d))Σ_Φ h_Falt(E,Φ). Lift both members of each reflex pair to a common CM Galois closure and count inverse embeddings.
Apply the induction scaling and linear ht, then sum over product factors.

nodes.title: CM Breuil–Kisin comparison
nodes.statement: For N_p as above, the integral Breuil–Kisin module M(N_p,y) is tensor-compatible. nodes.title: The standard CM quadratic line
nodes.statement: For H₀=E, let V₀={f∈End_Q(E):f(ax)=āf(x)}. Write f_a(x)=a x̄; then f_a∘f_a is multiplication by aā. Its filtered realization has Hodge line ω₀=Fil¹V₀,dR on Y₀. Equip this line with ||z||²=|[z,z̄]₀|, where [,]₀ is the bilinear form of Q₀. Compute composition and polarize the norm to obtain the hermitian and rational forms.

For T=T_x let Cl(T)=T(Q)\T(A_f)/T(Ẑ), I=[T(Ẑ):K_x], S={p:p|[O_x:R_x]}, and r_T:Cl(L)→Cl(T) the normal-closure reflex action. This is the inequality used in Tsimerman (2012), (4)–(5), pp. 17–18; its bad-prime loss must be absorbed, not dropped.

conventions.heights: h_Falt uses the unscaled squared volume metric; h_YZ=h_Falt+(g/2)log(2π). Both are additive logarithmic heights. Period-coordinate H_abs is absolute multiplicative Weil height; analytic h₀ is separately named.
conventions.fields: E/F is maximal-order CM of degree 2g in the averaged formula; g≥1 and all 2^g types, including imprimitive ones, occur. A general CM point uses its full center order R_x, one center-field factor per distinct simple isogeny class, with D_x=|disc R_x|.
conventions.degrees: AGHMP arithmetic degrees are divided by the matching weighted complex degree; CM component heights divide by [K:Q]; quaternionic h_L divides by [F(P):F]. Absolute polarized coarse moduli degrees and relative marked reciprocity orbit sizes are distinguished.
conventions.functions: CM class functions are locally constant and factor through finite quotients; conductor evaluation is a linear functional on this domain, with no continuity/measure claim. Total-height linearity has domain H_CM, the proper overlap span. A functional on full CM⁰ requires the component-period normalization; its uniqueness cannot be inferred from total heights.
conventions.proofRoutes: CMH.9 has alternative proofs. Its prerequisite union records both planned branches. Either fully verified branch suffices mathematically; no individual Colmez conjecture or Artin holomorphy conjecture is assumed.
